title: Prostate anatomy: zones, ducts and urethra
description: Prostatic zones and the urinary–ejaculatory crossing: urethra, verumontanum, ducts, seminal vesicles and erectile bodies.

questions.question: Where is the prostate located?
questions.answer: The prostate sits below the bladder and surrounds the first part of the urethra. Ducts from the reproductive tract open into the prostatic urethra.

questions.question: What are the main anatomical zones of the prostate?
questions.answer: The transition, central and peripheral zones differ in location and surrounding structures. The peripheral zone occupies much of the posterior gland.

questions.question: What is the bladder neck / internal sphincter?
questions.answer: Smooth-muscle outlet superior to prostate. Function: Closes during emission to limit retrograde ejaculation.

questions.question: Where is the prostatic peripheral zone located?
questions.answer: Posterior-lateral zone palpable through rectum. Function: Produces prostatic secretions.

questions.question: What is the function of the prostatic urethra?
questions.answer: Function: Conducts urine and semen in separate phases. Urethra through prostate from bladder neck to membrane.
